note: The four design directions explored for P1 (2026-07-23). "The Instrument" was chosen; see DESIGN.md. The other three are seed material for the repo-wide design review scheduled after P2.

proposals.philosophy: "The Instrument." This experience is a precision reading device, not a poster. Research is presented the way a scientific instrument presents a measurement: a value, its tolerance, and the grade of the probe that took it. The confidence interval is the hero mark — never a bare number. Restraint is the aesthetic: austere, ruled, data-forward, but warm enough to read for pleasure, like a well-set financial essay printed on engineering graph paper. Cognitively, the design is built on the encoding hierarchy (position for the point estimate — the most accurate channel; length for the CI band; motion-amplitude as a redundant preattentive channel for uncertainty), and on honest framing: nothing here resolves to a false point when the evidence is a band. You are meant to FEEL how much we do not know — the width of the band is the emotional payload, and every scene protects it.
proposals.one_line_pitch: A precision reading instrument for a trillion-dollar question — every claim shown as a value with error bars, where the width of the uncertainty band, not the headline number, is the thing you feel.

palette.name: Graphite Bezel
palette.role: Primary dark surface (dark-mode background / light-mode ink). A warm near-black — the color of an oscilloscope bezel, never pure #000. Carries phosphor-style amber/cyan traces at night.

palette.name: Bone Grid
palette.role: Primary light surface (light-mode background / dark-mode ink). Warm engineering-paper ivory that holds faint 8px gridlines. Never cold white — this is the warmth that makes an austere instrument readable for pleasure.

palette.name: Zinc Rule
palette.role: The instrument's scale: axes, gridlines, tick marks, whisker caps, secondary/label text, disabled states. Mode-neutral mid-gray that recedes so data reads first (low cognitive load).

palette.name: Filament Amber
palette.role: PRICE — the market-set, human-chosen number and the scarcity signal (warm). Point estimate is a crisp full-opacity tick; the 80% CI is a ~14% amber band. Brightens to ~#F2B04A as a trace on Graphite; darkens to ~#B87A19 for amber text on Bone.

palette.name: Cathode Cyan
palette.role: COST — the physical serving floor, the silicon (cool). Same tick-plus-band grammar as amber. Amber-vs-cyan is deliberately the single most colorblind-safe hue pair, reserved for the load-bearing distinction; the gap between them literally reads as a temperature gap between a human price and a physical cost.

palette.name: Redline
palette.role: Capital risk ONLY: the unresolved payback shortfall, the redline zone on the payback gauge, the reservoir of capex that never earns itself back. Single-use alert, never a routine category, and redundantly coded with a 45-degree hatch + text label so protanopes never confuse it with amber.

type.display: Martian Mono (Evil Martian, OFL) — a wide, engineered, variable monospace used for the big numbers, the proposition indices T1–T6, axis titles, and multiples (7x, 36x/yr, $1T). Numerals are the protagonists of this story, so the display face is a readout, not a headline.
type.body: Newsreader (Production Type, OFL) — a variable, screen-optimized serif with optical sizing, carrying the plain, short prose. It reads like long-form financial journalism: warm, literary, but with a faintly mechanical newsprint precision that keeps it out of cozy-blog territory.
type.mono: IBM Plex Mono (IBM/Bold Monday, OFL) — inline data values, tooltips, source grades (A/B/C), CI numbers, and terminal chrome, where Martian Mono is too wide to be legible.
type.rationale: The instrument has two voices and both are monospaced (display numerals + data chrome); the single human voice is a warm serif for connective prose. This deliberately INVERTS the generic pattern (serif hero over sans body) — here a humble serif sits beneath a monospace display on graph-paper Bone. It makes numerals the heroes (correct for an economics-of-intelligence piece), delivers reading pleasure through the serif, and touches none of the flagged generics (no Inter, no Space Grotesk). Three variable fonts are subset and preloaded to protect the static-site payload.

proposals.motion: Motion is the settling of a needle, not decoration. Two easings only: SETTLE (a critically-damped ease-out, cubic-bezier approx .16,1,.3,1, minimal overshoot) for any value snapping to its measured position, like a galvanometer arriving; and SWEEP (near-linear) for lines that draw on left-to-right via stroke-dashoffset, like a chart-recorder pen where the x-axis IS time. Particles never float, drift, or bounce — they snap to positions with a stagger ordered by data value, so a distribution 'resolves' like a scan. The one persistent, load-bearing motion is MEASUREMENT JITTER: at idle, each mark vibrates within its own 80% CI with amplitude proportional to CI width — wide, foggy estimates visibly shimmer; A-grade, tight estimates sit dead still. This makes uncertainty a preattentive channel you can feel across a whole field at a glance, redundant with the band's length. Scene transitions are scroll-driven, one change at a time (highlight OR annotate, never both), each morph ~600–900ms on SETTLE. prefers-reduced-motion fully replaces jitter with a static hatched band and swaps morphs for cross-fades — the meaning survives without the movement.
proposals.unit_metaphor: One particle is a single calibrated unit of measurement — a 'quantum' of value that keeps its identity as it changes role. The field is a fixed population of ~1,000–1,600 units (moderate, per the data-scale note; craft over raw count). A unit's scale is re-labeled per scene (one billion dollars in the capital scenes; one cent-per-million-tokens in the price scenes; one forecaster's estimate in the panel), but its constant identity plus position memory is exactly what makes the morphs legible, and its jitter-amplitude (= its CI width) travels with it everywhere, so uncertainty is a property of the matter itself. TRANSITION A — 'Cost becomes Price' (the gap): units first stack into the cyan marginal-cost band, shimmering inside the wide cost-model CI. On scroll, six of every seven units LIFT and re-stack ABOVE the cost floor to reach the amber US list price — the 7x gap is not asserted, it is built in front of you from the very same units that were cost. TRANSITION B — 'Capex becomes Revenue-needed' (the climax): the ~$1T of capex sits as units in vintage strata (sediment bands by build-year, a stratigraphic column). At the payback moment each capex unit must earn ITSELF back — it morphs and migrates onto the cumulative-revenue-needed curve toward 2030; units that find no revenue position inside the forecast cone fall into the Redline reservoir. Because it is the same unit you watched get built as a datacenter, you feel the bet in your gut: this exact dollar has to come home.
proposals.hub_concept: The hub is 'The Bench' — the research tree rendered as an instrument signal-flow schematic, not an org-chart or an illustrated tree. The two podcasts (Stratechery, Acquired) are PROBES on the left, each drawn as a live oscillating input trace. The two projects (P1 Economics, P2 Ad Market) are MEASUREMENT MODULES in the center that the probe signals patch into; each module shows a tiny live readout (P1: 'claims 160 - verdict 4 supported / 1 partial / 1 unresolved', with the price–cost-gap sparkline). The synthesis (P3) is the MASTER READOUT on the right where the module outputs combine. Edges are signal lines drawn like plotter traces (SWEEP easing on first load). It is a D3 DAG under the hood, styled as a lab patch bay, and it grows the obvious way an instrument grows: you patch in a new probe or bolt on a new module and the schematic extends. The same particle field lives behind the bench — hovering a module pulls a thin stream of that project's units forward as a preview, so diving in and returning feels like the same continuous instrument, never a page swap.
proposals.signature_interaction: 'The Convergence Dial.' One instrument fader labeled compute supply vs demand, dragging from SCARCE to ABUNDANT, teaches the entire thesis causally. As you drag toward abundant, the amber price units descend toward the cyan cost floor and the shaded amber 'scarcity umbrella' above cost shrinks in real time. The crucial honest move: the cost floor is a WIDE, jittering CI, so price never converges onto a line — it converges INTO a fog. You viscerally learn that 'marginal cost is back' does not mean marginal cost is KNOWN; convergence lands you in a band, not a point. At full abundance the readout flips: 'margin approaches 0 — now, does the $1T ever pay back?', handing you straight to the capital question. Two presets ride the same dial: US CLOSED (umbrella up, price floats far above cost) and OPEN WEIGHTS (umbrella collapses, price snaps into the cost band instantly) — the Kimi K3 near-controlled experiment as a switch, proving China prices near marginal cost not because its inference is cheaper but because open weights invite competing hosts. One control, and you have felt scarcity premium, the mechanism of convergence, the irreducible cost uncertainty, and the payback pivot.
p1_scene_beats: CALIBRATION (curiosity): the instrument powers on. The 160 calibrated claims arrive as a field of units, each a tick with an 80% CI whisker and a grade glow (A crisp, C faint, jitter-amplitude = CI width). They settle from noise into a quiet grid. Copy teaches the reading grammar before any argument: 'Every number here is a measurement, with error bars. Here is what we can and cannot see.' Uncertainty is established as first-class.

THE READING — price vs cost (T1, gap opens): zoom to one measurement. US list price per million tokens (amber) beside estimated marginal serving cost (cyan, wide band). Run TRANSITION A: cost units multiply upward ~7x to become price. The gap is constructed from the same units, not claimed.

THE HARD FLOOR (T2, supported): to prove the gap survives a foggy cost estimate, replay the real 80% price cut on an unchanged model — price units drop 80%; the model didn't change, so cost is AT MOST here. A solid cyan lower-bound rule locks in under the wide cost band. Lesson: even without a precise cost, the gap can't be explained away.

TWO CLOCKS (T3, contradiction that must coexist): per-token price collapses ~36x/yr at constant quality while the flagship price RISES 4x. Two plotter pens draw from the same unit stream and split — one diving, one climbing. Both true at once: AI is getting cheaper AND the frontier costs more.

THE CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT (T4, China vs US): Kimi K3 priced at a US rate before its weights shipped, then cheap once hosts competed. Flip the Convergence Dial's OPEN WEIGHTS preset: the umbrella collapses, price snaps into the cost band. Open weights, not cheaper silicon, drive price to marginal cost.

THE UMBRELLA AND CONVERGENCE (T5, tension peaks): the full Convergence Dial. Drag scarce to abundant; price descends into the jittering cost band; margin approaches zero. If convergence is coming, the premium that funds the whole buildout evaporates — the trillion-dollar bet comes into view.

THE PAYBACK CLIMAX (T6, unresolved — honest verdict): run TRANSITION B. ~$1T of capex in vintage strata must earn itself back by 2030. Cumulative capex vs cumulative-revenue-needed under a widening uncertainty cone, with a bear/base/bull DCF spread. Monte-Carlo units that find revenue = P(payback); the rest fall into the Redline reservoir. The verdict is a probability, not a yes/no, and the piece ends on the felt width of the cone.
proposals.why_not_generic: A lazy designer hits the AI-viz defaults: a purple-to-blue gradient, glowing neural-net filaments, a neon-green 'hacker terminal' in dark-mode-only, Inter or Space Grotesk, and decorative particles doing aimless Brownian confetti drift. For the argument they'd draw single-value bar charts (hiding uncertainty), truncate the y-axis to dramatize the 7x gap, render the hub as a clip-art org-chart or a literal illustrated tree, and close the payback question with a confident yes/no. I refuse each: warm graph-paper Bone plus a warm oscilloscope Graphite instead of neon; amber/cyan complementary traces (colorblind-safe, temperature-coded to human-price vs physical-cost) with a single hatched Redline for risk instead of a rainbow; Martian Mono numerals + Newsreader serif prose + Plex Mono chrome instead of any named generic, inverting the usual serif-hero pattern. Motion only ever encodes data — units snap to measured positions on a needle-settle ease, and idle jitter-amplitude equals CI width, so nothing moves for decoration. The CI band is the hero mark, so no number is ever shown without its error bars; axes are zero-based and honest; convergence lands in a fog, not on a line; the hub is a signal-flow bench (probes to instruments to readout), not a tree drawing; and the climax is a probability with a visible, felt uncertainty cone. And note the near-miss: warm-cream-plus-serif is itself a flagged cliche — I dodge it by making the monospace the dominant voice, keeping a co-equal dark 'oscilloscope' mode, and ruling the whole layout like engineering paper, so it reads as an instrument, not a cozy blog.
proposals.risks: Austerity can read as cold or intimidating; the warmth (serif prose, Bone paper, generous rhythm) must be actively defended or the piece becomes a Bloomberg wall that repels the lay reader it wants. Measurement-jitter is powerful but dangerous: too much amplitude looks glitchy or 'broken/loading', can cause visual fatigue, and must be throttled, capped, and fully killed under prefers-reduced-motion. Three variable fonts (two monos plus a serif) risk payload and FOUT on a static GitHub Pages site — subset and preload are mandatory. The cross-scene object-constancy morphs re-scale the unit population (split/merge tweening); if that mapping isn't legible the 'same dollar' story collapses into mere reshuffling, so the morphs need explicit anchor units the eye can track. The Convergence Dial risks implying determinism ('prices WILL converge') stronger than the evidence supports — framing must stay conditional to remain honest. Colorblind safety holds for the amber/cyan workhorse pair, but Redline sits near amber for protanopes, so it must stay single-use and carry hatch + label redundancy. Finally, making numerals the heroes (Martian Mono) risks readers anchoring on point estimates and missing the uncertainty thesis — the CI-first reading grammar has to be taught hard in Beat 1 (Calibration) so the band, not the number, is what people carry away.

proposals.philosophy: The Flow System. The AI economy rendered as a live engineering schematic: capital and tokens are discrete particles pumped through a value chain (Nvidia to clouds to labs to users), pooling into reservoirs where margin is captured and draining through valves where competition competes it away. Object constancy is literal and load-bearing: one dollar-particle enters as capex and you follow that exact particle until it either returns as revenue or evaporates. The governing metaphor is hydraulic, not merely electrical: money is a fluid, margin is pressure held above a floor, "scarcity" is a valve, and marginal cost is the floor the fluid settles onto when the valve opens. Two engineering-drawing traditions fuse: fluid dynamics (flow, pressure, pooling, laminar-vs-turbulent regimes) and orthographic schematic precision (dimension lines, callouts, instrument gauges). Crucially, uncertainty is built into the physics rather than annotated on top: an 80% confidence interval is a particle's turbulence, and a source grade is its crispness. The system is honest because you can never drain a price below a floor that is itself drawn as a fog band, not a line.
proposals.one_line_pitch: Follow one dollar of AI capital as it flows through the machine, watch where the market lets it pool into margin and where it drains to the cost floor, then find out, as a probability and not a promise, whether it ever flows back.

palette.name: Graphite Ink
palette.role: Structural ink: all schematic linework, dimension lines, and body text in light mode. Flips to become the canvas ground in dark mode. A near-black with a petrol/teal cast, deliberately not warm and not pure black, so the whole system reads as cool drafting stock rather than a glowing techno UI.

palette.name: Drafting Pale
palette.role: Ground: the drafting-paper canvas in light mode; flips to hairline grid, streamlines, and text in dark mode. A cool green-gray off-white, chosen specifically to avoid the banned warm cream. It is the neutral field against which a single hot particle is preattentively obvious.

palette.name: Brass Capital
palette.role: The thermal HOT pole. Encodes capital, margin, pricing power, capex particles, and every held-high price column. Amber reads as molten money being poured in and as the caution/bet register. Where flow pools into a reservoir the amber deepens in saturation; this is the color of captured margin.

palette.name: Coolant Teal
palette.role: The thermal COOL pole. Encodes the marginal-cost floor, commoditized/competed-away flow, and China's near-marginal pricing. Named for the coolant that carries heat off a chip: when margin drains, particles cool from Brass to Coolant. The amber-to-teal axis is the entire thesis rendered as temperature.

palette.name: Alarm Vermilion
palette.role: Reserved strictly for risk: the one unresolved proposition, the capex-revenue shortfall that may never close, valve over-pressure warnings, and particles that fail to return. A muted engineering vermilion used sparingly so its rarity carries weight. It is the color of the trillion-dollar question.

palette.name: Uncertainty Fog
palette.role: The uncertainty medium. Fills every 80% confidence-interval band, the widening forecast cone toward 2030, and the vapor of particles that evaporate when capital does not come back. Neutral and desaturated so it never competes with signal, but always present so no number is ever drawn as falsely exact.

type.display: Bricolage Grotesque (SemiBold/Bold, variable, SIL OFL, self-hosted)
type.rationale: The spine of the pairing is aerospace instrumentation. B612 and B612 Mono were commissioned by Airbus for aircraft cockpit displays, engineered for legibility of critical readouts under stress. That is exactly the register the Flow System wants: a trillion-dollar bet stated in the calm, high-legibility voice of an instrument panel, not a blog. B612 carries the plain short sentences that must hold serious ideas (it passes the grade-10 gate at small sizes by design), and B612 Mono, with tabular figures, sets every calibrated estimate, 80% CI, source grade, dollar figure, and axis tick so numbers align honestly in columns. For contrast, display uses Bricolage Grotesque, a modern grotesque with structural, machined letterforms (flat apexes, engineered ink traps) that stamp the six propositions like nameplates without decoration. This deliberately avoids the AI-generic Inter and Space Grotesk while keeping a coherent technical-instrument world: expressive-but-engineered display over a neutral cockpit body and a tabular readout mono. (If a harder, more schematic display voice is wanted, Chakra Petch is the aggressive alternative; Bricolage is the readable default.)

proposals.motion: Advection, not decoration. Particles never teleport and never bounce; they are carried along a flow-field through channels, the way a real fluid moves. Scroll is the pump: scrolling sets the flow rate, and when the reader stops, flow eases to a slow idle drift because capital is never fully at rest. Four motion primitives carry meaning. (1) Laminar vs turbulent encodes confidence: narrow-CI grade-A streams flow smooth and parallel; wide-CI grade-C streams spread and eddy, with jitter amplitude proportional to CI width, so uncertainty is felt as turbulence rather than read from an error bar. (2) Pooling and draining encode margin: where the market lets margin accumulate, particles slow, density rises, a reservoir fills and the amber deepens; where a valve opens, particles accelerate, thin out, and cool from Brass to Coolant as they fall to the floor. (3) Morphs are re-routings: scene changes send the same particles through the flow-field to new roles with per-particle stagger, so a block never rigidly slides; the fluid reads. (4) Settling is critically damped: releasing a pressure column drops it and settles onto the floor with no overshoot, because this is engineering precision, not playful spring. Easing is cubic in-out for macro transitions (roughly 400 to 900ms); ambient advection is continuous but slow. A first-class reduced-motion mode replaces flow with static streamlines and arrowheads, renders CIs as still fog bands, and turns morphs into crossfades, so the schematic remains fully honest and legible without motion.
proposals.unit_metaphor: One particle is one billion dollars of capital, a dollar-drop, in the money scenes, and one quantum of served intelligence, a token-drop, in the pricing scenes. Because the buildout is roughly $1T-plus, that is on the order of one to a few thousand particles: moderate count, canvas/WebGL-friendly, where craft matters more than raw scale. A particle is never a bare dot. It carries a horizontal CI halo whose width is the 80% interval, a crispness set by source grade (A crisp, B soft, C fuzzy), and a flow regime (laminar or turbulent) that encodes confidence. Object constancy is carried across named transitions. TRANSITION 1, Capex to Revenue (the payback loop): a dollar-drop is born hot and amber at the top of the chain as Nvidia/cloud capex, advects down through clouds and labs to users, and in the climax the chain bends into a closed loop where each capex drop must complete the circuit and return as a revenue drop. The cumulative-capex curve IS the stacked reservoir of these very drops; the cumulative-revenue-needed line is the drain they must refill by 2030. Drops that make it back glow as returned capital; drops that do not evaporate into Uncertainty Fog and drift off the top, so you literally watch how many billions may never come home. TRANSITION 2, Cost to Price to Margin (the gap): one token cost-drop rests on the Coolant-Teal marginal-cost floor; the US list price is that same drop with six amber margin-drops stacked above it into a held column, the roughly 7x gap, propped by a valve labeled scarcity umbrella. The hard lower bound (an 80% price cut on an unchanged model) is the valve cracking once: the column drops about 80% and settles to a level still above the teal floor, proving margin remained. When supply later catches demand, those same amber margin-drops drain and cool to teal. TRANSITION 3 (bonus), Kimi K3: one model's token-drops priced at the amber US rate before weights ship; the instant open weights release, competing host-channels open and the same drops re-route and cool to the near-marginal teal floor. Same particles, same model, so the price fall is visibly caused by multiplying channels, not by cheaper Chinese inference.
proposals.hub_concept: The living research tree is drawn as a piping-and-instrumentation schematic, a watershed of capital rather than a botanical tree. Two source reservoirs, the podcasts Stratechery and Acquired, feed two process stations, P1 Economics and P2 Ad Market, which flow into a confluence vessel, P3 Synthesis: five top-level nodes, respecting working-memory limits and Hick's Law. The schematic sits on Drafting Pale ground in Graphite Ink, with a slow ambient drift of idle particles through the trunk lines so the tree is alive even at rest. Hovering a node opens an instrument readout (claim count, average source grade, status). Clicking a project pumps you into that branch: the camera follows the flow down the pipe and dives into the self-contained P1 scrollytelling essay. Returning surfaces you back to the tree with the P1 branch now marked flowed (valve open, reservoir partly drained), giving a persistent you-are-here state via recognition rather than recall; a miniaturized version of this schematic rides along as a minimap during the essay. Growth is designed into the aesthetic: the schematic shows ghosted, capped stubs where future branches (P4 and beyond) will graft, an honest under-construction signal that is part of the engineering-drawing language rather than a disclaimer. The hub is simultaneously the sitemap, the mental model, and the repo-wide design system reference.
proposals.signature_interaction: The Scarcity Valve. A single draggable valve on the main pipe between labs and users, paired with a pressure gauge, labeled compute supply vs demand. It teaches the entire thesis in one gesture. At the start (supply below demand, scarcity high) the valve is nearly closed: price sits about 7x above the Coolant-Teal cost floor as a tall amber column held under pressure, and the gauge reads high, meaning high margin. As the reader drags the valve open, amber margin-drops drain out of the column, the price column falls and cools toward teal, the pressure gauge drops, and in concert the China/Kimi line and the per-token collapse animate downward. Two honesty constraints are wired into the physics: the column can never fall below the floor, and the floor itself is a fog band, not a line, so the reader cannot pretend marginal cost is exact. At full open a readout resolves: prices converge to marginal cost across US and China alike, so the only question left is payback, which hands directly to the climax. Cognitively it is a Norman-grade actionable model: direct manipulation with immediate multi-channel feedback (position and length carry price at the top of the Cleveland-McGill hierarchy, temperature carries margin-vs-cost, the gauge is redundant feedback, the fog band enforces honest uncertainty). One control lets the reader feel that markup is a function of scarcity, not geography or true cost, covering T1 through T5 and setting up T6.
p1_scene_beats: Beat 1, Intake: Follow one dollar (curiosity). The value-chain pipe (Nvidia to clouds to labs to users) is drawn as a clean schematic on Drafting Pale. One hot amber dollar-drop enters at the top and flows through; you watch where it pools and where it thins. Establishes the unit, the flow, and object constancy. Preattentive hook: a single hot drop on a cool schematic. This is the emotional on-ramp before any number.

Beat 2, The Gap (the widening gap). Zoom to the labs-to-users stage. The token-serving cost rests on the teal floor; the US list price is a tall amber column about 7x above it. The gap is shown two honest ways at once: the wide uncertain cost-model band drawn in Uncertainty Fog, and the hard lower bound proved by the 80% price cut on an unchanged model (the valve cracks; the column drops but stays above the floor). Teaches T1: the marginal cost of inference is back, and the gap is real. The floor carries an explicit CI band.

Beat 3, Two curves that disagree (deepening tension). Per-token price collapses roughly 36x per year at constant quality WHILE the flagship price rises 4x. Two streamlines share one channel moving opposite ways: a cooling teal stream draining down (per-token, quality-held) and a heating amber stream climbing (flagship frontier). They coexist without contradiction because the schematic shows they measure different things. Teaches the subtle proposition that a falling unit price and a rising flagship price are both true.

Beat 4, The controlled experiment: Kimi K3 (mechanism revealed). The identical model is priced at the amber US rate before its weights ship; the instant weights release, competing host-channels open and the same drops re-route and cool to the near-marginal teal floor. The same-particle morph makes the causation legible: price falls because open weights invite competing hosts, not because Chinese inference is cheaper. Teaches T4, framed explicitly as a near-controlled experiment, never as a bare cause arrow.

Beat 5, The Scarcity Valve (the interactive fulcrum). The reader is handed the valve and drags supply to catch demand, watching price converge to the uncertain cost floor across US and China alike, with the pressure gauge falling. This is the aha that unifies T1 through T5 in one manipulable model. It closes by surfacing the last open question, payback, and pumping the reader into the climax.

Beat 6, The trillion-dollar loop (tension to climax). The chain bends into a closed loop. Cumulative capex (~$1T-plus in vintage bands) stacks as a reservoir of amber drops; the cumulative-revenue-needed line is the drain they must refill by 2030, with a widening Uncertainty-Fog cone forecasting forward and a bear/base/bull DCF spread shown as three loop-closure rates. The superforecaster panel appears as scattered independent markers, disagreement shown as spread rather than averaged into one number. Drops that fail to return evaporate into fog and the shortfall glows Alarm Vermilion. This is T6, the unresolved proposition that carries all the capital risk, answered as a probability, not a yes or no.

Beat 7, The verdict readout (honest, uncertain close). A final instrument panel shows the six propositions T1 through T6 as valves and gauges: four fully open and steady (supported), one half open (partly), one flickering Alarm Vermilion (unresolved). The verdict is stated as a calibrated probability with its CI. The reader is invited back to the research tree with the P1 branch marked flowed. Honest close: the gap is real; whether the bet pays off is a probability, not a promise.
proposals.why_not_generic: A lazy designer handed this brief does five predictable things. One, draws a static Sankey diagram of the AI value chain in default D3 category colors, which has no object constancy, no uncertainty, and hides margin inside a labeled band. Two, makes a literal blueprint: cyanotype blue background, white lines, monospace everything, glow, the cliche of every engineering-themed landing page. Three, reaches for purple-to-blue gradients, glassmorphism, and neon particle sludge, the fintech/crypto default the brief explicitly bans. Four, renders the payback climax as a single line-crossing of capex versus revenue with a confident yes/no, erasing the very uncertainty that is the point. Five, ships Inter or Space Grotesk plus a warm serif on cream, and buries uncertainty in error bars no one reads. The Flow System avoids each deliberately. The dead Sankey is replaced by a live fluid you follow one drop through, where margin is emergent (pooling) rather than a static label. The blueprint cliche is subverted into cool Drafting Pale and Graphite Ink stock rather than cyanotype blue, with a semantic thermal palette where margin is heat (amber) and cost is cool (teal), so color means something instead of decorating. Uncertainty is promoted to first-class and preattentive: a CI is a particle's turbulence, source grade is its crispness, the forecast is a widening fog cone, and payback is a probability, so the honest four-supported/one-partial/one-unresolved verdict is the entire payload, not a confident single line. Typography borrows the voice of aerospace cockpit instruments (B612) so every number reads as a high-stakes readout, with a tabular mono keeping CIs honestly aligned. And the thesis is not asserted but made manipulable through the Scarcity Valve, so the reader concludes it by feeling the pressure drop themselves.
proposals.risks: Risk 1, flow soup: if advection dominates, the particle field becomes pretty but unquantifiable and readers miss the encoded magnitudes. Mitigation: always pair the WebGL particle layer with a crisp D3 overlay (axes, direct labels, gauges) so position and length carry the real numbers; particles are the emotional layer, D3 is the measurement layer. Risk 2, motion-encoded uncertainty misreads as glitch or noise and can fatigue or exclude motion-sensitive users. Mitigation: cap jitter amplitude, teach the laminar-vs-turbulent legend once, and ship a robust reduced-motion mode (static streamlines, arrowheads, still CI bands, crossfade morphs). Risk 3, the thermal amber-to-teal plus vermilion scheme must survive color-vision deficiency and the hot-equals-margin mapping is arbitrary until taught. Mitigation: redundant encoding (position, label, gauge, and hue together, never hue alone), a one-time legend, and WCAG-checked contrast in both light and dark modes. Risk 4, the hydraulic metaphor can imply false mechanical precision or false causation (valve opens, therefore price falls, as if certain). Mitigation: fog bands on every floor, probability framing at the climax, explicit near-controlled-experiment labeling for Kimi K3, and no bare cause arrows. Risk 5, performance: WebGL particles plus D3 overlays plus scroll on static GitHub Pages must hold 60fps on mid laptops with roughly one to four thousand particles and morphs. Mitigation: moderate particle counts (units in the thousands per the brief), instanced rendering, per-scene precomputed flow-field targets, and scroll throttling. Risk 6, hub legibility as the tree grows. Mitigation: cap top-level nodes at five, ghost future branches as capped stubs, and keep the schematic as a persistent minimap so new research grafts on without overwhelming the reader.

proposals.philosophy: The Essay — a definitive magazine feature that happens to breathe. Typography is the protagonist and carries the argument; visualizations are set like full-bleed photographic plates in a print feature, not embedded widgets. This is a deliberate division of cognitive labor (Mayer's multimedia + modality principles): prose is the serial channel that carries the causal reasoning — WHY open weights invite competing hosts, WHY a scarcity umbrella holds price above cost, WHY a falling price and a rising price can both be true — while charts are reserved for the one thing text is bad at: magnitude comparison. Particles are atmospheric ink over the page until a scroll beat crystallizes them into a plate of evidence, then they dissolve back into prose. Emotion comes from pacing, whitespace, and typographic drama, never from decoration or spectacle. The reader should feel they are reading the definitive piece on this question — Stratechery's argument, set like a beautifully printed book, paced like The Pudding — and should leave trusting it precisely because it never oversells the numbers.
proposals.one_line_pitch: A print-grade long-read on whether AI's trillion-dollar bet ever pays back — where the prose reasons and grains of ink, crystallizing out of the page's atmosphere into full-bleed plates, do the measuring, and the verdict arrives as an honest probability rather than a promise.

palette.name: Pressroom Ink
palette.role: Primary ink / body text in light mode; full-page surface in dark mode. A near-black with a cool blue-green undertone (not pure #000) so long-read text is easy on the eye and the dark surface reads as dried ink, not screen-black.

palette.name: Cold-Press Paper
palette.role: Page surface in light mode; primary text color in dark mode (paper-white printed on ink). A cool archival cotton-paper tint with a faint sage-grey cast — deliberately NOT warm cream, to signal serious broadsheet over cozy blog.

palette.name: Cinnabar
palette.role: PRICE. US list price, the premium line, the scarcity umbrella, heat and the risk of the bet. Dark-mode lift: #E15236. Historically an expensive pigment and the color of red ledger ink — semantically 'marked up.'

palette.name: Petrol
palette.role: COST. The marginal serving-cost floor and the proven lower bound; cool, factual, the honest baseline. Dark-mode lift: #35A0B4. Paired against Cinnabar as a red-vs-blue contrast that is maximally preattentive AND colorblind-separable (protan/deutan safe).

palette.name: Brass
palette.role: CAPITAL. Cumulative capex vintage bands, the trillion-dollar bet, and the marker for the single unresolved proposition (T6). Dark-mode lift: #D2A64E. A muted antique gold — money without tackiness.

palette.name: Fog
palette.role: UNCERTAINTY and structure. Confidence-interval bands, the widening forecast cone, gridlines, axes, secondary type. Desaturated so it recedes — the salience budget is spent on the data and the three ink accents, not the chrome (Tufte data-ink; attention economy).

type.display: Fraunces (variable) — high-contrast old-style serif with attitude, run at large optical sizes (48–120px) with a touch of its WONK/SOFT axes for editorial personality. It carries the emotional headlines and the scene turns; its optical-size axis lets the same face be dramatic at display and calm at deck.
type.body: Newsreader — a serif engineered for sustained on-screen reading at ~20px/1.6, set to a 62–66 character measure. It gives the long-read book-like gravitas so plain, short, grade-<=10 sentences look authoritative rather than thin. It is a deliberate serif-on-serif system with Fraunces, separated by contrast-of-contrast (Fraunces high-contrast and wonky; Newsreader even and quiet).
type.mono: IBM Plex Mono — the instrument voice, used only for numbers: every calibrated claim's estimate, its 80% CI, its A/B/C source grade, dollar figures, x-multiples, token counts. Chosen for true tabular figures so CIs and dollar columns align to the digit (honest numeric comparison depends on this), and for an engineered neutrality that reads as 'readout' rather than 'prose.'
type.rationale: Three faces = three cognitive channels, each signposting a reading mode so the reader never confuses argument with measurement (reduces mode-switching load): dramatic display serif for affect and orientation, quiet reading serif for the sustained causal argument, tabular mono for quantities. It pointedly avoids the AI-generic Inter/Space-Grotesk pairing and the warm-cream-plus-generic-serif cliche; the drama lives in setting and scale, not in exotic vocabulary, which keeps the prose inside the readability gate while the type still feels grand.

proposals.motion: Motion language: 'Settling Ink.' Every data unit is a fine grain of ink suspended over the page in one of two states — DIFFUSE (atmospheric, low-opacity Brownian drift, the resting texture of the essay) or CRYSTALLIZED (snapped to an exact position inside a plate). The transition between them is a settling, not a slam: decelerating ease (cubic-out / low-tension spring) so grains 'settle like sediment' or 'ink drying,' ~600–900ms, generous and reading-paced, never appy. Scroll is the only clock — nothing autoplays, nothing parallaxes for its own sake; the reader's scroll is the deterministic timeline, which keeps them in control and lowers cognitive load. Typographic drama is animated through Fraunces' variable axes: a headline can gain weight and contrast as it settles into place, so emotion is delivered by type, not by effects. Crucially, motion encodes uncertainty honestly: a settled central estimate that is well-known (grade A) comes to rest crisp and still; an uncertain one (grade C) keeps a residual shimmer, breathing within its Fog CI band — motion magnitude = uncertainty, a preattentive channel no static chart has. Full-bleed rhythm: when a plate crystallizes, the text column yields to a full-frame plate that then 'prints' its axes and annotations; after the beat it recedes and columns resume, like turning to a photo plate in a magazine and back. All of this degrades under prefers-reduced-motion: crystallization becomes a cross-fade, jitter becomes a static Fog band with a legend, and the essay remains fully readable with zero animation.
proposals.unit_metaphor: One particle is a GRAIN — a single quantum of the thing the current plate measures, whose canonical incarnation is one dollar of money in the AI economy at billion-dollar granularity (so ~$1T of capex is ~1,000 grains: moderate count, craft over scale). Grains never teleport and never pop in or out; because they move continuously, the reader's perception binds them across scenes (Gestalt common-fate + continuity), so the money FEELS like the same money moving through the whole argument — object constancy is the emotional engine. Named transition 1, 'Price becomes Cost' (the gap plate): ~700 grains crystallize into one vertical stack = the US list price of a million tokens (Cinnabar). As the prose explains marginal cost, that exact stack splits — roughly one-seventh of the grains settle low as Petrol COST, and the other six-sevenths lift and hover as the GAP/margin. The 7x is never a number you read; it is the ratio of grains you watched separate on a common baseline (Cleveland–McGill length-on-a-scale, the most accurate encoding). Named transition 2, 'Capex becomes Revenue' (the payback climax): the hovering margin grains flow right and re-aggregate into the cumulative capex mountain in Brass vintage bands; then, to answer 'does it pay back?', each Brass capex grain that gets earned back must physically cross over and re-color as a Revenue grain climbing under the revenue-needed line to 2030. The dollar of capex you watched get built IS the dollar that must be earned back — the unresolved proposition is literally the grains that never make it across in the base case. (Reprise transition: the China/Kimi-K3 controlled experiment reuses the same grains, sitting high as US-priced Cinnabar until weights ship, then cascading down to the Petrol floor — identical grains, identical model, re-priced only by competition.)
proposals.hub_concept: The hub is 'The Stemma' — the masthead and living family-tree of a serial publication, built from the same grains as the essays. The landing is a full-bleed masthead: 'The Economics of Intelligence' set huge in Fraunces, and behind/beneath it a quiet particle field organized into a research lineage. Two dense grain-clusters at the roots are the source podcasts (Stratechery, Acquired); their grains flow up the trunk into two feature branches (P1 Economics, P2 Ad Market) and converge into a synthesis crown (P3). It is overview-first (Shneiderman: overview -> zoom -> details-on-demand): a visitor sees the whole tree, then selecting a branch pulls its grains forward and prints its title plate. The layout is a tree/force hybrid designed to accrete — new projects simply grow new branches, so the design system scales as the research tree grows. Object constancy operates at repo scale: the grains that form the P1 branch ARE the grains that become the atmosphere of the P1 essay, so entering a project is a continuous zoom into its branch and returning is the grains receding back into the tree. Each project's grains carry its palette identity (P1 = Cinnabar/Petrol/Brass), so the whole repository reads as one continuous particle world with a persistent 'return to the tree' spine as breadcrumb.
proposals.signature_interaction: 'Fold the Umbrella' — one draggable control on the central gap plate that lets the reader perform the entire thesis with their own hand. Two settled quantities sit on a common baseline: PRICE (Cinnabar, high) and COST (Petrol, low, drawn as a Fog band because the cost model is uncertain, plus a solid Petrol rule marking the HARD lower bound proven by the 80% price cut on an unchanged model). Between them hover the GAP grains — the margin under the scarcity umbrella. The reader drags a single handle labeled 'US compute supply: scarce -> abundant.' As they pull toward abundant, the Cinnabar price line descends toward the Petrol floor and the GAP grains drain away — teaching 'when compute supply catches demand, prices converge,' as a physical act rather than a sentence. The payoff twist: the drained margin does not vanish; those exact grains flow off to the side and stack into the Brass capex mountain — the very act of competing the margin away is what produces the trillion-dollar bill that must be earned back, handing the reader straight into the payback question. A preset button, 'What China did (open weights),' snaps the handle to show open weights as a shortcut to the same convergence for an identical model — collapse without cheaper inference. The whole control is reversible and annotated as an illustrative coupling (not a causal law), and because price descends into a band and stops at the proven hard bound, the interaction teaches the uncertainty as faithfully as it teaches the mechanism. This is embodied learning (generation effect + direct-manipulation feedback loop): you cause the convergence, so you remember it.
p1_scene_beats: Beat 1 - Curiosity, 'A number that shouldn't exist': full-bleed page of diffuse ink grains; a big Fraunces line poses the hook (a million tokens costs you $X; serving it costs the lab about $X/7). One grain lands early with its Fog CI band and an A/B/C grade to teach the reader that every number here carries its own uncertainty. Grains begin to gather.

Beat 2 - The gap crystallizes, 'Seven to one' (T1/T2 supported): grains snap into the split stack — Cinnabar price vs Petrol cost vs the hovering margin — so 7x is read as a length ratio on a shared baseline, not a counter. The 80%-price-cut hard bound prints as a solid Petrol rule, proving the gap is real even while the cost model stays an honest band.

Beat 3 - The paradox, 'Falling and rising at once': the plate morphs to a dual time-line — per-token price collapsing ~36x/year (Petrol, plunging) sitting together with the flagship headline price rising 4x (Cinnabar, climbing). Annotation resolves it (quality-per-dollar collapses; the frontier product is repriced up), modeling honest framing instead of cherry-picking one curve.

Beat 4 - The controlled experiment, 'The same model, two prices': China vs US. Identical model (Kimi K3) sits high as US-priced Cinnabar before its weights ship; when weights ship and hosts compete, the SAME grains cascade to the Petrol floor. The near-controlled experiment shows open weights — not cheaper inference — cause the collapse.

Beat 5 - The signature interaction, 'Fold the umbrella': the reader takes the supply handle, drives US price toward the cost floor, and watches the drained margin grains flow off and begin stacking into capex. Diagnosis turns into the bet; tension begins.

Beat 6 - The climax, 'Does it pay back?' (T6 unresolved, all the capital risk): the Brass capex mountain assembles in vintage bands (~$1T+) and races a cumulative revenue-needed line to 2030 under a widening Fog cone, with a bear/base/bull DCF spread. Capex grains try to cross over into revenue; in the base case some never make it. The superforecaster panel appears as scattered markers — the disagreement itself is the signal, never averaged into one false number.

Beat 7 - The honest verdict, 'A probability, not a promise': the answer resolves to a probability distribution with an explicit interval, not a yes/no. The grains settle into that distribution but keep a faint residual breath — the irreducible uncertainty made visible. A calm closing Fraunces line, and a quiet return-to-the-tree affordance.
proposals.why_not_generic: A lazy designer would reach for the AI-startup starter kit: Inter + Space Grotesk, a warm-cream page with a generic serif, a purple-to-blue gradient, and glowing neon dots floating in a dark void. I use a print-ledger ink-and-paper system (Pressroom Ink on cool Cold-Press Paper, never cream), Fraunces/Newsreader/IBM Plex Mono, and three semantic ink accents (Cinnabar/Petrol/Brass) with no gradient blobs; the particles are ink grain on paper, not glowing nodes in space. Lazy would animate the '7x gap' as a number counter ticking up, or exaggerate it with two bars on a truncated axis — I encode it as a physical split of the SAME grains on an honest shared baseline and prove the floor with the 80%-cut hard bound rather than a single flattering cost estimate. Lazy would hide uncertainty behind point numbers and a smooth confident forecast line to 2030 — here uncertainty is the native unit: CIs as Fog bands, the forecast as a widening cone, superforecaster disagreement shown as scatter not a mean, residual particle jitter encoding confidence, and a verdict delivered as a probability. Lazy would autoplay parallax spectacle with a dozen colors and 3D chartjunk — I make scroll the only clock, hold to two particle states and a strict six-color role system, and keep every plate flat and honest. And lazy dark mode is an inverted stylesheet — mine is a purpose-built dual palette with lifted accent variants and paper-white text printed on ink. Even the hub avoids the default rainbow force-graph: it is an editorial stemma built from the same grains, palette-coded and overview-first.
proposals.risks: Serif-on-serif (Fraunces + Newsreader) can go muddy if the contrast and voice are not aggressively separated — mitigated by strong size/contrast difference and using mono as the clear third voice, but it needs disciplined type QA. Object constancy is the whole emotional bet and it is the hard engineering: grains must keep stable identity across seven scene morphs (keyed joins / persistent GPU buffers) so they never teleport; moderate counts (~1–2k) help, but choreographing the morphs is the real craft cost and the main schedule risk. Motion-as-uncertainty (jitter = CI) is elegant but can read as jank or annoy, or be misread as random noise — must always be paired with an explicit Fog band and legend and fully replaced under prefers-reduced-motion. 'Fold the umbrella' risks implying false precision, as if dragging supply deterministically sets price — it must be annotated as an illustrative coupling, land price into a band, and stop at the proven hard bound, never asserting a causal law. Full-bleed plates plus long-read columns can cause pacing whiplash on small screens, and particle fields tax low-end devices — needs canvas fallbacks, reduced counts, and static plate images for the no-JS/static-site baseline. The Essay leans on type carrying emotion while prose must stay at grade <=10 with short sentences — if drama is chased through vocabulary the readability gate breaks, so drama must come only from setting, scale and pacing. Finally, Cinnabar-red reads as 'danger/loss' and could be misread as a naive profit/loss cliche against blue — prevented by redundant direct labels, the split-stack semantics, and choosing red/blue specifically for colorblind separability.

proposals.philosophy: "The Reckoning." A tension-forward, cinematic direction built around one bet: roughly a trillion dollars of compute capital going in against a return no one can yet promise. The whole experience is engineered like a foundry and a courtroom — capital is minted, poured, and accumulated into looming masses, then called to account. Emotion comes from scale, contrast, and consequence, never from doom-mongering or hype. The climax is not a verdict of "bubble / not bubble" but a settling of accounts expressed as a probability (the panel's 56%), with its uncertainty shown honestly and dramatically rather than smoothed away. Reckoning is the perfect double meaning for this subject: it is literally the computation of accounts, and it is the moment stakes arrive. The design makes both meanings visible at once. I commit to this fully — high contrast, weight, and stakes — and deliberately reject the calmer, more neutral registers the other directions would take.
proposals.one_line_pitch: A trillion dollars, minted particle by particle behind a scarcity umbrella, races the revenue it must earn back by 2030 — and the finish line is a probability, not a promise.

palette.name: Furnace Black
palette.role: Dark-mode ground and light-mode ink. The high-contrast anchor; a cool near-black with a slate cast, like an unlit foundry or a ledger before it is filled. Everything dramatic is staged against or drawn in this.

palette.name: Cold Steel
palette.role: Unearned capital: capex particles, the accumulating mass, the money already committed but not yet returned. A mineral, industrial steel-teal chosen precisely because it is NOT the generic tech blue — it reads as cold, hard, poured metal that has not yet been lit. Mode-tuned lighter (#5A93A6) on Furnace Black so it glows rather than sinks.

palette.name: Molten Gold
palette.role: Earned-back value: revenue, ignited particles, the payoff. The foundry-glow hue. When a capex particle is overtaken by revenue it flashes toward a white-hot crest (#FFF3D6) then settles to this gold. In light mode, amber TEXT deepens to #B8701A for contrast; the #F2A63C stays for fills and particle bodies.

palette.name: Ash Grey
palette.role: Write-downs and the muted register: capital left unearned past the horizon, secondary labels, dimmed UI, depreciation. A cool neutral grey that works identically light or dark. Semantically it is the color of consequence without alarm — value that quietly did not come back.

palette.name: Ember Red
palette.role: The rationed alarm. Used ONLY for the single unresolved proposition (T5) and the shared top risk (OpenAI counterparty solvency / the un-earned overhang). Never decorative, never for generic emphasis. Because it is the only saturated warm-danger hue in the system, the one red node is preattentively unmissable — the trillion-dollar risk is visible from orbit. Mode-tuned to #D9503E on Furnace Black.

palette.name: Cool Vellum
palette.role: Light-mode ground and body text on dark. In dark mode it also draws the faint ledger rules, axes, and gridlines — the accounting scaffold behind the drama. A cool paper-white, explicitly NOT a warm cream, to keep the whole system severe and broadsheet-like rather than cozy.

type.mono: Martian Mono (Medium; tracking tightened for dense tables)
type.rationale: Display — Archivo Expanded is a grotesque on a width axis, so its headlines and giant figures ($1,070,000,000,000) feel carved into a vault wall: monumental mass, not decoration. I exploit the width and weight axes semantically — the biggest stakes render literally widest and heaviest, a direct size-encoding of magnitude (Cleveland & McGill: length/size is a strong quantitative channel, here borrowed for type). It is the opposite of an ultra-condensed movie-ticker; The Reckoning is about looming MASS, so an expanded face beats a condensed one. Body — Newsreader is a screen-first broadsheet serif with true optical sizes and financial-journalism gravitas, ideal for a long scrollytelling read; a serif signals serious research-as-media, and its cold, newsy character deliberately avoids the warm humanist-serif-on-cream cliche the brief bans. It carries plain, short, grade-<=10 sentences with authority. Mono — Martian Mono's grid-locked, engineered forms read like an instrument panel and a countdown clock: perfect for the live payback counter, the 80% confidence intervals, source grades A/B/C, and the $/token tape. Its tabular figures anchor exact, honest numbers beside the impressionistic particle field, so the drama never floats free of the data. All three are open-source and static-site friendly; none is Inter, Space Grotesk, or a purple-gradient default.

proposals.motion: Motion language: WEIGHT and CONSEQUENCE. Capital has inertia, so masses move slowly with ease-out settling and a faint overshoot-then-rest, as if heavy metal is being poured and stacked; moments of reckoning are sudden — a fast-attack, slow-decay ignition flash like a struck bell or furnace flare. The contrast between slow accumulation and abrupt settling IS the emotional engine. Everything is scroll-linked and scrubbable (deterministic, reversible) — the user operates the timeline; nothing autoplays past their control, which paces cognitive load (Mayer's segmenting). Transitions between scenes are MORPHS, never cuts: particles travel curved paths to their next role and the on-screen count is conserved, so you can watch the same grains restaff — visible conservation is honest design. Uncertainty is felt, not stated: particles jitter within their 80% CI band as a slow, low-amplitude shimmer, so a wide band literally looks unstable; hover or lock a claim and the jitter freezes to the point estimate — motion = uncertainty, stillness = certainty. Write-downs never explode; they desaturate to Ash and drift downward in a restrained ash-fall. Source grade is encoded by edge sharpness (A = crisp, C = soft/hazy) — blur is preattentive and intuitively maps to "fuzzy evidence." One salient motion at a time: the background holds still while the focal transformation plays, so attention is never split. A prefers-reduced-motion mode swaps physics for cross-dissolves and static CI bands while conserving every meaning.
proposals.unit_metaphor: One particle is a grain of capital-at-stake — a hard-edged, faintly luminous shard (an ingot seen edge-on, not a soft dot; The Reckoning wants mineral weight, not confetti). The canonical spine budget is 1 grain = $1 billion, so the ~$1.07T buildout resolves to ~1,000 grains: a legible, monumental mass rather than an abstract number. Object constancy means the SAME grains persist and change role, color, and position across scenes; the dollar denominator is relabeled on-screen in mono at each zoom (an honest denominator, so the metaphor never silently lies). Two named transitions carry the spine: (1) THE POUR / MINTING — the margin grains from the price-vs-cost gap (the charged empty space between the 7-high price stack and the 1-high cost floor) do not dissipate; they stream downward and pack into the capex vintage strata (2023 -> 2024 -> 2025 -> 2026), changing role from scarcity-rent to capital-at-risk and color from Molten Gold toward Cold Steel. The margin that the umbrella earns becomes the capital the industry commits. (2) THE RECKONING / EARN-BACK — those Cold Steel capex grains detach from the accumulated mass and are chased by a rising cumulative-revenue-needed line toward 2030; each grain the revenue line overtakes ignites to Molten Gold (earned), while grains still un-reached past the 2030 horizon desaturate to Ash and drift down (written down). The same grain that was a dollar of margin, then a dollar of capex, ends as either earned gold or ash — you watch its whole fate without a single grain appearing or vanishing arbitrarily.
proposals.hub_concept: The Reckoning Tree — the landing hub is a single living capital-flow tree rendered in the exact same particle field as the essays, so the whole repository feels like one continuous field you navigate rather than a menu. At the base, two source springs (Stratechery, Acquired) feed grains upward. Two trunks rise from them — P1 (The Economics of Intelligence) and P2 (the ad market) — each a luminous accumulating mass whose height encodes claim count (P1 today = 160 calibrated claims) and whose color-mix encodes verdict distribution: Molten Gold for supported propositions, Cold Steel for the still-open, Ember Red for the ones carrying capital risk. The two trunks converge into a crown — P3, the synthesis. Because Ember Red is rationed system-wide, the single unresolved, capital-bearing node (P1's T5) glows red on the tree and is visible from the first frame: a visitor sees the entire risk landscape before reading a word. Structurally this is a clean hub-and-spoke with progressive disclosure (only ~6 nodes, well inside 7+-2): hover a trunk to preview its headline verdict as a probability ("Does the buildout pay back? 56%"); click to dive, and the chosen trunk's grains carry you into that essay's Scene 1 (object constancy from hub to story); a return breadcrumb re-forms the tree at the branch you left. The tree is built to grow — new branches (future projects, new podcast sources) graft on without redesign, and the whole thing is honest at a glance about what is settled versus what is still at stake.
proposals.signature_interaction: "The Scarcity Umbrella" — one draggable control that teaches the entire thesis. On screen: a price stack (~7 grains tall) held aloft above a cost floor (1 grain) by a visible umbrella labeled SCARCITY; to the right, the capex mass and a revenue-needed line; a mono readout of price/token, cost/token, margin, and live payback probability. The user drags a single slider from "supply scarce / one host" toward "supply abundant / many hosts." As they drag, the umbrella dissolves and the price grains fall and compress toward the cost floor — the ~7x gap collapses toward ~1x. Critically, the falling margin grains do not vanish: they stream into the capex mass (object constancy — margin is what funds the buildout), so as the margin thins the revenue line visibly falls short and an Ember-Red earn-back gap opens. A second toggle, "ship the weights," runs the real controlled experiment: Kimi K3 sits at the US umbrella price ($15/M output, identical to Claude Sonnet) with weights unreleased; flip the toggle and the SAME unchanged model's price drops to the cost floor as competing hosts appear — proving the cut is competition, not cheaper Chinese inference. In three seconds of dragging, the user feels: (1) the price-cost gap is scarcity rent, not cost; (2) open weights or supply catch-up collapse it; (3) a collapsing margin is exactly what threatens the trillion-dollar payback. This is direct-manipulation causal learning (Norman): you build the correct mental model by operating the mechanism, not by reading a paragraph about it. Grains are conserved throughout, so the lesson is also honest.
p1_scene_beats: BEAT 1 — ONE GRAIN (curiosity, establish the unit). Open on a single Molten Gold grain against Furnace Black: this is what you pay for when you buy AI — value, priced per token. A mono tape reads the price. Zoom out: a task is a swarm of grains. We teach the color code immediately on this one grain (gold = value/earned, steel = capital, red = risk, ash = written down) so the language is learned before it is loaded. Low load, one idea, a concrete human hook: the price you actually pay.

BEAT 2 — THE GAP (the widening question). The price stack rises to ~7 grains; the cost floor holds at 1. Scroll widens the charged empty space between them. We show the gap two honest ways per the evidence: a wide, shimmering cost-model band (particles spread to their 80% CI — the honest 2x-16x uncertainty, edge-sharpness = source grade) AND a hard, crisp lower floor proved by the o3 cut ('80% off, same exact model'). Zero-based, conserved units — no truncated axis theatrics. Curiosity turns to tension: why is price sitting so far above cost?

BEAT 3 — THE UMBRELLA (mechanism; the signature interaction). Scarcity is named as the thing holding price up. The reader drags the Scarcity Umbrella and flips 'ship the weights' on Kimi K3, learning that the gap is scarcity rent and that open weights — not Chinese geography — collapse it. Folded in here: the two contradictory curves shown as two grain streams from the same field diverging — constant-quality price collapsing ~36x/year while the flagship input price RISES 4x to $5. Both true at once; the umbrella leaks but has not broken.

BEAT 4 — THE POUR / MINTING (tension materializes; named transition A). Follow the margin. The margin grains from the gap stream down and pack into the capex vintage strata (2023 -> 2026), changing from gold to Cold Steel — margin becomes committed capital. The mass grows to a monumental Archivo figure: ~$718B big-four in 2026, ~$1.07T across the world, ~$1.4T of OpenAI commitments behind it. Scale becomes dread made physical: the trillion-dollar bet, poured grain by grain.

BEAT 5 — THE OVERHANG (stakes; the unresolved proposition). Pull back to the full looming Cold Steel mass, which casts a shadow sized to the revenue it must earn back (Cahn's ~$1.5T bar). The six propositions appear as verdict nodes: T1, T2, T4, T6 ignite gold (supported); T3 half-lit (partly / refined by Kimi K3); T5 pulses Ember Red — unresolved, and carrying all the capital risk. Everything now rests on the one red node.

BEAT 6 — THE RECKONING / EARN-BACK (climax; named transition B, the race). The capex grains detach and are chased by a rising cumulative-revenue-needed line toward 2030. The uncertainty cone fans wide (spread = honest uncertainty), with bear/base/bull catch-lines. The three superforecasters appear as scattered markers — 27% / 56% / 61% — the DISAGREEMENT shown as signal, its ~25-point spread traced to one modelling choice (pro-rata vs scarcity-years revenue). Grains the revenue line overtakes ignite gold; grains past the 2030 horizon fade to Ash. Chips earn at the frontier ~3.9 years but are booked over 5-6 — the timing squeeze made visible. Resolves as a probability, a mono counter settling on 56%, not a yes/no.

BEAT 7 — THE LEDGER / RETURN (honest denouement; hub return). Grains settle into a final reckoning: payback probability 56% with its CI, source grades, and the load-bearing uncertainty named in plain words (the revenue-attribution choice; OpenAI counterparty solvency as the shared top risk — the one thing that would move the verdict most). No false certainty, no doom. Then the grains lift and re-form the Reckoning Tree, returning the reader to the hub and pointing toward P2 and P3 — the same grains that carried the whole story now waiting to grow the next branch.
proposals.why_not_generic: A lazy designer handed 'AI economics' reaches for the same kit every time, and I refuse each move deliberately. (1) They would default to a purple-blue gradient, glassmorphism, and Inter/Space Grotesk; I use a foundry palette (Furnace Black, Cold Steel, Molten Gold, Ash, rationed Ember Red) with Archivo Expanded / Newsreader / Martian Mono — a severe, engraved, broadsheet system tied to the actual subject: silicon foundries, poured capital, molten-vs-cooled metal, ledgers. (2) They would draw a dual-axis price-vs-cost line chart with a truncated y-axis to make the 7x gap look scarier; I render the gap in conserved, zero-based grain units and prove it two honest ways (a wide CI cost band AND the hard o3 '80% off, same model' floor), so drama never comes from a distorted axis. (3) They would collapse the ending into a clickbait 'Is AI a bubble? YES' verdict; I keep it a probability (56%) with a visible widening uncertainty cone and forecaster disagreement shown as scatter, because the honest finding IS a coin flip. (4) They would scatter decorative particle 'confetti' that maps to nothing — literal chartjunk; every grain here is a conserved dollar of capital whose count is preserved across each morph, and motion encodes uncertainty and source grade rather than sparkle. (5) They would lean on doom (crashing red arrows, a bursting bubble) or hype (rockets, glowing brains); I ration Ember Red to the single genuinely unresolved risk (T5) and render write-downs as quiet ash-fall, so the piece feels consequential without editorializing. (6) They would show single-number point estimates for false precision; here the 80% CI is the native visual unit, blur encodes A/B/C source grade, and the superforecaster spread is the headline, not the noise.
proposals.risks: 1) Drama-vs-honesty tension: a cinematic, high-contrast register can tip into editorializing doom or manufacture false certainty about a bearish outcome. Mitigation: ration Ember Red to the one real unresolved risk, keep the verdict a probability with full CIs, and foreground forecaster disagreement (27/56/61) rather than a single scary number. 2) Spurious conservation: the margin -> capex -> revenue morph could imply a literal 1:1 dollar identity that the economics does not support. Mitigation: relabel the dollar denominator on-screen at every zoom, mark illustrative flows as stylized, and hold the quantitative scenes (the gap, the payback race) strictly to-scale and zero-based, visually separated from the impressionistic transitions. 3) Object constancy at moderate particle counts: if a scene needs more or fewer grains than the last, conservation visibly breaks. Mitigation: fix the canonical budget (1 grain = $1B), and render any merge or split explicitly with a labeled scale change rather than silently spawning grains. 4) Performance: a WebGL particle field plus scroll-scrubbing can jank on mobile and low-end devices. Mitigation: Canvas-2D fallback, level-of-detail on grain count, and a reduced-motion mode that swaps physics for cross-dissolves and static CI bands while conserving meaning. 5) Cognitive overload: many co-existing complexities (price collapse vs flagship rise, six propositions, a DCF spread, a forecaster panel). Mitigation: one salient change per beat, progressive disclosure, and a persistent mono readout that anchors exact numbers so the field never floats free of data. 6) Accessibility of the palette: Molten Gold on Cool Vellum is weak for text and Cold Steel/Ember shift by mode; Martian Mono is dense in tables. Mitigation: mode-tuned tokens (deepened amber text, lifted steel/red on black), WCAG contrast checks, a always-visible mini color legend introduced on Beat 1's single grain, and tightened mono tracking for tabular data. 7) Learned color semantics: steel/gold/ember/ash must be taught before they are loaded; if a reader enters mid-scroll the code is opaque. Mitigation: teach the full code on the very first grain and keep a small persistent legend anchored throughout.
